The words

How sweet the name of Jesus sounds
In a believer’s ear!
It soothes his sorrows, heals his wounds,
And drives away his fear.

It makes the wounded spirit whole,
And calms the troubled breast;
’Tis manna to the hungry soul,
And to the weary rest.

Dear name! the rock on which I build,
My shield and hiding place,
My never failing treasury filled
With boundless stores of grace!

By Thee my prayers acceptance gain,
Although with sin defiled;
Satan accuses me in vain,
And I am owned a child.

Jesus! my shepherd, husband, friend,
O prophet, priest and king,
My Lord, my life, my way, my end,
Accept the praise I bring.

Weak is the effort of my heart,
And cold my warmest thought;
But when I see Thee as Thou art,
I’ll praise Thee as I ought.

Till then I would Thy love proclaim
With every fleeting breath,
And may the music of Thy name
Refresh my soul in death!

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Eb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on s (B♭), on the word “How”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

John Newton published these words in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book 1, number 57, under the heading “The name of Jesus”. The tune ST. PETER is by Alexander R. Reinagle.

  • Words (1779): John Newton (1725–1807)
  • Music (1826): Alexander R. Reinagle (died undefined)

Tune ST. PETER by Alexander R. Reinagle (died undefined); words by John Newton (1725–1807).

Questions about How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds

What is the doh of How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds start on?

It starts on s (B♭ in Eb major), a pickup on the word “How” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to s.

Is How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds in the public domain?

Yes. John Newton died in 1807, Alexander R. Reinagle died in undefined; the words were first published in 1779 and the music in 1826. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
